newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
GALE CHAOS ON ROAD AND RAIL

Meteorologists have said that yesterday's storm, the worst since the hurricane of 1987 was the tail end of Hurricane Lili which hit the Caribbean last week. As winds exceeded 90 mph, devastation was wrought across the south east where at least four people have died.
LLOYD'S FACES HUGE TWA BLAST CLAIMS

The Lloyd's of London insurance market could be liable for up to 1.2 billion pounds from the explosion of TWA Flight 800 off Long Island in New York. The U.S. investigators of the incident are thought to be on the verge of concluding that mechanical failure was to blame, a verdict which could lead to huge product liability and negligence claims against Boeing and TWA, and big losses for the Lloyd's syndicates which insured them.

Yasuo Hamanaka, the trader at the centre of the Sumitomo copper scandal, will plead guilty to charges that he forged a signature on a document purporting to give him full authority to trade copper for Sumitomo. However, he may still implicate Sumitomo's senior management in his courtroom testimony.
DOLLAR CLIMBS ON U.S. TREASURY CHIEF'S WORD
The dollar soared to 114.9 yen, following comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that he is relaxed about the greenback's recent rise.

India is undergoing a property boom as a direct result of the country's market reforms which have attracted multinational companies and joint ventures. Property costs are on a level with London and Tokyo as rents and purchase prices have doubled in the past year.
